news.title: BMC panel to decide fate of 3,169 trees for Dharavi redevelopment & infrastructure projects in Mumbai
news.para: Mumbai's Tree Authority will consider proposals impacting 3,169 trees on Tuesday.  Permissions are sought to fell 1,777 trees and transplant 1,392 others for development.  The Dharavi redevelopment project seeks to remove 1,693 trees, with compensatory planting planned.  Other projects include a tunnel, IIT housing, and a slum rehabilitation scheme.  These decisions come amid growing scrutiny over tree removal for infrastructure.

news.title: Mumbai: BMC panel to consider leasing 15-acre Mulund dump land for Dharavi redevelopment works
news.para: The BMC plans to lease fifteen acres of reclaimed land at Mulund dumping ground. This land will be used by Dharavi Redevelopment Project for a casting yard. The civic body expects to earn over one hundred crore rupees in rent. The developer will manage site remediation and obtain necessary environmental clearances. This proposal will soon be presented for approval by the Improvement Committee.

news.title: Telangana grants special relaxation for commercial high-rise in Jubilee Hills
news.para: Hyderabad government approved special concessions for a commercial building construction.  The high-rise will be permitted extra height and other building rule relaxations.  This special case allows construction up to thirty meters with additional floors.  Applicants will surrender land for road widening free of cost.  The order follows examination of representations and municipal reports.

news.title: Greater Bengaluru authority notifies building approval fee structure
news.para: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has issued a new fee structure for construction approvals. Fees will now be calculated using site guidance values and built-up area. Inspection fees vary for residential and non-residential building types. Basic amenities and environmental impact fees are set for a five-year license period. Issuing plinth certificates also has a newly notified fee structure.

news.title: Jaipur development body flags 6,000 illegal commercial units on residential plots
news.para: Jaipur Development Authority will submit an audit to the Supreme Court.  This audit identifies over six thousand commercial establishments operating illegally.  The Supreme Court previously directed authorities to survey such residential violations.  JDA will present findings and enforcement actions taken by August fourth.  Officials face scrutiny for compliance and preventing unregulated commercialization.

news.title: Kerala RERA awards buyers 16.65% interest for delayed flat handover
news.para: Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority ordered a builder to pay homebuyers interest.  The authority mandated 16.65% simple interest for delayed flat possession.  This order mandates the builder to complete amenities and execute sale deeds.  The builder cannot use demonetisation or floods to justify the significant delay.  The project remains unfinished, causing considerable distress to the overseas buyers.

news.title: Haryana RERA orders builders to pay compensation to buyers for delays in flat handover
news.para: Haryana Rera ordered builders to pay homebuyers compensation for delayed project possession.  In one case, a buyer received over Rs 40 lakh for significant delays.  Another buyer received additional compensation for delayed physical handover.  The authority rejected developer arguments about double penalties for delays.  These rulings reinforce homebuyers' rights to compensation for developer failures.

news.title: Flat registrations frozen; Nagpur civic body takes over NIT plan approvals
news.para: Flat registrations in Nagpur are suspended until further orders. Builders must now verify infrastructure and safety compliance for occupancy certificates. The Nagpur Municipal Corporation will approve building plans for former Nagpur Improvement Trust layouts. This move aims to streamline development approvals and eliminate overlapping jurisdictions. The future of the Nagpur Improvement Trust is under consideration by the government.

news.title: NGT directs verification of continuing 'illegal' construction in Greater Noida
news.para: The National Green Tribunal has directed the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board to verify allegations. Some under-construction projects in Greater Noida allegedly continue despite closure orders for environmental violations. The tribunal is hearing a matter filed by BJP leader Rajendra Tyagi regarding these projects. The Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority is also examining details of these alleged violations.

news.title: Mumbai: Pattathu Brothers' directors booked for failing to hand over amenities to housing society
news.para: According to a complaint lodged by an SRA assistant engineer, Joseph S Pattathu and Pearl Joseph Pattathu, directors of Pattathu Brothers, allegedly breached redevelopment terms by failing to transfer possession of six required facilities to the eligible beneficiaries after securing completion certificates for the project.

news.title: Tower demolition plan in Bengaluru sparks OC debate
news.para: A Bengaluru apartment tower faces demolition after structural instability was detected. This incident raises serious questions about the credibility of occupancy certificates issued by the Greater Bengaluru Authority. Experts highlight a disconnect between regulatory approvals and actual structural safety assessments. Concerns are also resurfacing regarding construction on vulnerable lakebeds and marshy terrain. Citizens demand greater accountability from regulators and developers for building safety.

news.title: Retailers lease 4.1 million sq ft Grade-A mall space in H1 2026: Report
news.para: India’s top seven cities recorded gross leasing of 4.1 million sq ft of Grade-A mall space in H1 2026, against new completions of 0.9 million sq ft, according to Anarock. Grade-A mall vacancy declined to 6.7%, the lowest level since 2010.

news.title: Indore: IMC issues fire safety directives to building owners, commercial establishments
news.para: To enforce compliance, IMC is conducting a city-wide inspection drive. Property owners or operators found misusing basements or rooftops in violation of National Building Code (2016) Part-4 standards and prevailing building bylaws and safety standards will face formal notices and legal action.

news.title: Thiruvananthapuram: Housing project in limbo, families left waiting
news.para: The Thanal Housing Project in Muttathara remains stalled, affecting nearly one hundred families. Fresh technical and cost hurdles prevent the contractor from commencing much-needed construction work. This delay also holds up the relocation of slaughterhouses operating opposite the colony. Residents continue living in deteriorating houses while awaiting permanent housing solutions. The newly elected corporation council plans a detailed review to decide the project's future.

news.title: Competing claims over geotechnical report emerge in SNN Raj Etternia case in Bengaluru
news.para: Nagadi’s Sept 2022 geotechnical report states that according to information provided by the client, a portion of the project site was a former quarry that had been filled with soil, debris, and other material. The report adds that the investigation was carried out keeping these site conditions in mind.

news.title: Women property registrations jump 45% in Chhattisgarh after fee slash
news.para: A cut in registration fees for properties bought in women’s names has pushed their share of registered deeds from 32% to 41% in just under two months, according to state data. The jump is not just statistical.

news.title: Strata deploys ₹96 crore in residential projects in Chennai, Bengaluru
news.para: Strata has made structured credit investments of ₹96 crore across three RERA-approved residential developments in Chennai and Bengaluru. The transactions are structured targeting returns of about 16-17% per annum.
